findings.title: Lane contract test permits Unit and Provider to be aliases
findings.finding: The test asserts only that both enum names exist. C# permits enum SessionLifeUnitGateScope { Unit = 0, Provider = 0 }; both Assert.Contains calls pass for that definition. The planned contract explicitly requires distinct Unit and Provider values, and aliased values cannot reliably discriminate the unit-only lane from the later provider lane.
findings.correction: Assert that the named Unit and Provider values are unequal after reflection, retaining name/type checks. Add this assertion before a new genuine contract Red run. This is a contract-shape correction, not a demand to implement lane behavior now.

findings.title: Consumer contract test accepts private instead of internal
findings.requirement: Reviewed internal static Build.ValidateSessionLifeUnitGate contract; test plan lines30,45-46
findings.finding: BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.NonPublic finds private methods as well as internal methods. The assertions never check MethodInfo.IsAssembly. A private static void ValidateSessionLifeUnitGate(ISessionLifeUnitGateValidator, SessionLifeUnitGateValidationRequest) passes this test even though Build.Tests cannot call it as the promised typed consumer boundary. The existing InternalsVisibleTo Build.Tests declaration grants internal access, not private access.
findings.correction: Assert exact internal accessibility (IsAssembly), static/non-generic shape, and the existing return/parameter contract. Keep the later typed mock-backed consumer test mandatory; do not use reflection invocation as a substitute for proving the promised typed boundary.

findings.title: Caller-owned project selection can evade the request-property blacklist
findings.requirement: TR-MCP-PLAN-001-AC002; no caller-maintained selected-project list; test plan lines28,32,44,59
findings.finding: The test requires five property names but rejects only six selected additional names. A request with all five required properties plus a public ExpectedProjects or ProjectNames collection passes unchanged. That is a caller-owned selected-project list under a different name, violating the explicit contract that inventories come from Nuke beneath the run root.
findings.correction: Validate the exact reviewed public instance-property set and types, or an equivalently complete assertion that rejects every caller-supplied selection surface. An exact five-property set is the smallest correction for this frozen contract. Do not add another project list to the caller or test harness.

findings.title: Single-operation interface assertion counts only methods named Validate
findings.requirement: Reviewed single validator operation; test source XMLDocs lines15-17 and test plan line29
findings.finding: Assert.Single(validatorType.GetMethods(), method => method.Name == Validate) proves exactly one matching Validate method, not that the interface exposes only the promised operation. An interface containing void Validate(request) plus void Reset() still passes. This is relevant to the stated single-operation boundary, not a new report-validation requirement.
findings.correction: Assert the complete exposed operation surface contains only the intended instance Validate operation, then check name, return type, and request parameter. Account for inherited operations if inheritance is permitted, or keep the reviewed interface declaration inheritance-free. Retain the xUnit2031-compatible assertion form.
